_recording.how: A `command` hook handler that appended its argv, its stdin and its environment to a JSONL file, plus the same script as the `notify` program. Runs were made in a throwaway git repo under /tmp with CODEX_HOME pointed at an isolated directory, so the user's own ~/.codex was never written to.
_recording.clients: hook payloads captured from both `codex exec` and the interactive TUI under a pty; they were identical. The `notify` payload differs between them only in `client`.
_recording.delivery: Hook payloads arrive on STDIN as a single JSON object. argv is empty: a handler `args` array parses but is silently ignored. The `notify` payload arrives as one extra argv entry appended after the configured arguments.
_recording.environment: The environment of the `codex` process is inherited by hook handlers and by the notify program; TURN_HOOK_URL and TURN_SESSION_ID were both observed arriving intact.
_recording.identifiers: Within one session the hooks' `session_id` and notify's `thread-id` were byte-identical (019fcdc4-5f91-7980-b743-11575462cd61 in the TUI run), so Turn has one external id whichever mechanism reports it. The payloads below come from several runs, so their ids differ between entries.
not_captured: PreToolUse / PostToolUse / PreCompact / PostCompact — accepted by the config parser and listed by `hooks/list`, but Turn does not subscribe to them so they were never exercised.

rejected_spellings.session_start: snake_case event keys are accepted by the TOML parser and then never match any event: `hooks/list` reports zero hooks
rejected_spellings.sessionStart: camelCase likewise parses and never fires; camelCase is the app-server wire spelling, not the config spelling
rejected_spellings.handlers: the per-matcher handler list key `handlers` parses and never fires; Codex calls it `hooks`, same as Claude Code
rejected_spellings.hooks=\"/path/file.json\": rejected outright: invalid type: string, expected struct HooksToml

handler_keys.type: command | prompt | agent — only `command` runs; `prompt` and `agent` warn "prompt/agent hooks are not supported yet"
handler_keys.command: executed THROUGH A SHELL: $HOME expands and globs expand, and an unquoted path containing a space fails outright. Must be POSIX-quoted.
handler_keys.timeout: seconds; default 600, clamped to 1 for SessionEnd
handler_keys.async: parses, then warns "async hooks are not supported yet"
handler_keys.args: parses and is silently ignored — argv reaches the handler empty

_config.file_form: $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json is also discovered, as {"description": …, "hooks": {<same PascalCase event map>}}, reported with source="user". The top-level object rejects unknown keys; nothing deeper does.
_config.oracle: `codex app-server` + a JSON-RPC `hooks/list` call reports every hook Codex actually parsed, with its trustStatus. It is the only way to tell a working config from one that parsed and will never fire.
_config.notify: notify=["/abs/path/turn-hook"] — an array of program and arguments, with the JSON payload appended as one further argument. The recording used a `--url http://127.0.0.1:PORT/hook/TOKEN` pair here and that is why the shape is known, but Turn must not: argv is world-readable (/proc/<pid>/cmdline), so the per-node token would be harvestable by any local account. The URL travels in TURN_HOOK_URL, which this recording also proved the notify program inherits.

_trust.summary: A freshly configured hook is `untrusted` and will not run.
_trust.codex_exec: Silently runs nothing. No warning, no error, no non-zero exit — the session looks entirely normal and zero callbacks arrive.
_trust.interactive_tui: Blocks at startup on a modal, transcribed verbatim from a pty capture: "Hooks need review / 7 hooks are new or changed. / Hooks can run outside the sandbox after you trust them. / 1. Review hooks / 2. Trust all and continue / 3. Continue without trusting (hooks won't run)"
_trust.granting: "Trust all and continue" appends to $CODEX_HOME/config.toml one entry per handler: [hooks.state."/<session-flags>/config.toml:<snake_case_event>:<matcher_index>:<handler_index>"] with trusted_hash = "sha256:…". After that `codex exec` runs the hooks with no extra flags.
_trust.invalidation: Changing the handler command flips trustStatus to "modified" and the review is required again. So Turn's helper path is part of what the user trusted.
_trust.bypass: --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust makes hooks run without trust and prints a warning twice. `codex app-server` does not accept the flag. Turn must never pass it: granting hook trust is the user's security decision.
_trust.notify_is_not_gated: With hooks left untrusted in a fresh CODEX_HOME, notify still delivered agent-turn-complete. notify has no trust gate.
